# Data-driven motion sample

The owner asked to see an actual video. `projects/fold-sample.json` is an original
agent-directed film for fictional FOLD, a pocket paper notebook. It introduces a
fleeting thought, the in-between moment, a writing action, the notebook and a held
ending. The green cover and all product artwork are illustrative designs, not
documentary photographs or supplied product geometry.

**This sample was directed by the ChatGPT agent. It was not generated by the
experimental local 4B/9B Director, and does not demonstrate an autonomous app
capable of arbitrary video requests.** The research proposals remained rejected.

## What is implemented

`render.py` executes a JSON scene graph with arbitrary scene counts and layer
compositions. Text, lines, rectangles, ellipses and polygons are reusable drawing
primitives. Position, rotation, scale, opacity, blur and reveals are keyframed.
Layered shadows give limited 2.5D depth. Product names, layouts, words and the
story live in the project file; there are no `if scene == 3` or product-category
branches in the renderer. A five-shot sample is a directed sequence, not a fixed
five-shot template used for every request.

The voice adapter synthesizes each narration line with the existing accepted M3
identity, its unchanged 0.98 speed and pinned Supertonic 3 assets. Cut durations
use actual saved WAV lengths plus explicit reading/hold time. An original sparse
plucked score and paper/ink/tap accents are synthesized from project data. The
1080×1920, 24 fps output uses H.264, AAC stereo, fast-start MP4 and output loudness
normalization. No paid service, borrowed creator footage or cloned voice is used.

## Reproduce

System packages: FFmpeg and `fonts-urw-base35`. Python drawing dependencies:
Pillow and NumPy. Voice dependencies: SoundFile, ONNX Runtime and the Supertonic
SDK. The measured environment used NumPy 2.3.5 and Pillow 12.3.0.

Pinned SDK:
`supertone-oss-archive/supertonic-py@df0f9686dac7fbbde391b759e2ee5286a3737622`.
Pinned weights:
`supertone-oss-archive/supertonic-3@aafc6e32416a594460b32413efc49d7fe4ce6d46`.
Download its `onnx/` files, config, license and `voice_styles/M3.json` into a local
model directory; weights are not bundled here.

```bash
python -m motion_studio.voice --project motion_studio/projects/fold-sample.json \
  --model-dir /path/to/supertonic-3 --out output/fold-sample
python -m motion_studio.render --project motion_studio/projects/fold-sample.json \
  --out output/fold-sample --width 1080 --fps 24
```

The output is `sample.mp4`; `render-manifest.json` retains measured timings and
direction provenance. Original per-shot WAVs remain available for voice checks.

## Acceptance boundary

This adds a real executable compositor for **authored scene graphs**, not an
automatic compiler from arbitrary prose. It does not implement real 3D, semantic
asset generation, automatic visual criticism or general natural-language-to-video
planning. A future Director must produce and validate this representation, resolve
assets and facts, and render/inspect its own output before claiming that ability.

Own code/artwork: project MIT license. Third-party dependencies retain their own
licenses. Supertonic inference code is MIT; the archived model weights use
BigScience OpenRAIL-M, not the code's MIT terms. URW base35 fonts are AGPL-3 with
the upstream font exception; the video contains rasterized text and no font files
are redistributed here. See the installed Debian package copyright and upstream
repositories for the full terms.
